name: Calling in the Reserves
summary: At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder sends you south to relieve a weary sentry at the Great Lift. He gives you a letter for Grish Longrunner, who has stood watch far from home.

sections.title: A Long-Awaited Relief
sections.body: Maggran Earthbinder keeps troop welfare and supplies in hand at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Across Kalimdor, the Horde strains to keep its garrisons staffed, even after the Third War. Maggran knows that endless watch duty wears seasoned soldiers down. So he sends a reassignment letter south to the Great Lift, where Grish Longrunner has stood guard far from home.

sections.title: Watching the Lift
sections.body: The Great Lift joins the southern Barrens to the canyons of Thousand Needles. With Maggran's letter in hand, Grish can leave his lonely watch over the lift mechanisms and return to his family. Fresh reserves can take his place.

aliases: where to get calling in the reserves
faq.answer: Maggran Earthbinder gives you the letter at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains.

faq.q: Where do I deliver Maggran's letter?
faq.answer: Take Maggran's Reserve Letter south through the Barrens to the Great Lift, above Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Why does Grish Longrunner need relief?
faq.answer: Grish Longrunner has watched the lift mechanisms alone for a long time. He asked to be relieved so he could travel home and visit his family.

faq.q: Is there any combat required for this quest?
faq.answer: No combat is required. You carry a message south toward Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Which faction gains reputation from completing this?
faq.answer: Delivering the letter grants you reputation with Thunder Bluff, whose tauren oversee the route.

faq.q: Where does this quest lead next?
faq.answer: The delivery brings you to the top of the Great Lift. You can ride it down into the canyons of Thousand Needles and explore more Horde outposts.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you see commanders rotate sentries across the Kalimdor frontier to keep morale high and watchposts steady.
As a tauren, you help keep the Great Lift passage open toward Thunder Bluff's wider territories.
